function: ResNet18 outputs hybrid RSMA precoders and combiners and the common-rate allocation vector of the UAV downlink, maximizing energy efficiency while approximating ideal SVD-based hybrid RSMA (pp. 6-9).
system: UAV with 16 or 36 antennas and 4 or 9 users of 4 antennas each; mmWave, 10 MHz, carrier not stated; external jammer; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: ResNet18 with four residual units and fully connected outputs; supervised training on SVD-ideal hybrid RSMA labels, loss merging objective and constraints, Adam; mandatory constraint module (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Self-generated Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels (5 clusters, 10 rays, random angles) with SVD labels; 40,000 training and 10,000 test samples; no standard dataset (pp. 3, 7, 10).
test_conditions: Train and test sets (40,000 and 10,000 samples) share one generator; antenna numbers, jammer distance, and maximum power are swept; no unseen scenario is tested (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: OMP-RSMA and MoAltMin-RSMA hybrid precoding; multiple access: ResNet18-NOMA and ResNet18-SDMA, which reuse the proposed ResNet18 with another scheme; no earlier learned precoder compared (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Energy efficiency and weighted sum rate versus jammer distance, maximum transmit power, and antenna numbers; training loss convergence (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Order formulas only: training O(E x I/B x sum of residual-block convolution costs), inference (O_M + O_A) x N; no numeric operations, parameters, or runtime (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 3: "We adopt a clustered channel model, known as the Saleh-Valenzuela model". Not met: a custom Saleh-Valenzuela simulator with random angles (Algorithm 1, p. 7), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 10: "we assess the performance of the proposed algorithm by varying the number of antennas, maximum transmission power, and the level of jammer interference." Not met: these are sweeps in one simulator; the paper never states a test on an unseen scenario or after adaptation (Table II, p. 10: 40000 training and 10000 testing datasets).
q3_support: p. 11: "MoAltMin-RSMA: Apply MoAltMin algorithm to optimize the hybrid RSMA matrices and select RSMA as the MA scheme [17]". p. 12: "ResNet18-NOMA: Apply the algorithm based on ResNet18 to optimize the hybrid RSMA matrices and select NOMA as the MA scheme [30]." Not met: the non-learned baselines (OMP, MoAltMin) are compared, but the ResNet18 variants are the proposed method, and no earlier learned precoder is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "The training complexity of the algorithm proposed in this" paper is given as O(E x I/B x sum of residual-block costs). p. 10: "the inference complexity of the proposed algorithm in this paper can be estimated as" (O_M(m) + O_A(m)) x N.
q5_support: p. 7: "the absence of standardized and general-purpose datasets highlights the necessity of developing datasets tailored to specific communication models and algorithms." Not met: the authors generate their own dataset and give no code or data link.
notes: Included as area 6 by the specificity order, because the learned ResNet18 controls the beams (hybrid precoders), power, and common-rate allocation of a UAV-to-ground link (pp. 7-9). Area 3 is the alternative reading (base station precoder) if the stationary UAV is treated as a plain base station; the reviewer should confirm. q4 rests on order-of-complexity formulas (pp. 9-10); the paper gives no numeric operations, parameters, or runtime. The ResNet18-NOMA and ResNet18-SDMA comparisons (p. 12) are variants of the proposed method, so they do not give the learned baseline of q3. The external jammer only enters the SINR (p. 5), and the learned function is hybrid precoding and rate allocation, so the anti-jamming exclusion was considered and not applied. Table II (p. 10) and Figs. 6-7 (p. 12) were read from page images.
